output.headline: Pays Everlast Development $9,200 to clear fire-risk vegetation at Thurgood Marshall Elementary School
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The text says "thirty (36) days," where the words and number disagree.
output.summary: The district hires Everlast Development Inc., the lowest responsive bidder in a competitive bid, to cut and remove brush and weeds, and trim bushes, ivy and low branches, along fences and across the grounds at Thurgood Marshall Elementary School, in line with the Oakland Fire Code. The amount is $9,200.00, which includes a $3,000.00 contingency (money set aside for unexpected costs). The work was scheduled to run from July 26, 2021 to August 31, 2021, before this approval.

output.headline: Adds $3,309.48 to Mar Con Builders' Acorn Woodland playground matting contract
output.summary: This change order adds $3,309.48 for installing rubber sheeting to prepare the site for playground matting at Acorn Woodland Elementary School. It raises the contract from $113,200.00 to $116,509.48 and extends the end date from October 31, 2020 to November 10, 2020. The contract term began September 16, 2020, before this approval.

output.headline: Adds $12,122.87 to Mar Con Builders' Global Family playground matting contract
output.summary: This change order adds $12,122.87 for an extra utility site scan, asphalt for the new playground location, and capping and filling a drain at the previous playground location at Global Family Elementary School. It raises the contract from $88,320.00 to $100,442.87 and extends the term by 212 days to May 31, 2021. The contract term began September 16, 2020, before this approval.

output.headline: Hires Atlas Technical Consultants for up to $49,908.10 of soil testing at Cole Administration Center
output.summary: The district hires Atlas Technical Consultants, LLC to provide geotechnical (soil and ground) engineering and observation services for the Cole Administration Center project. This includes reviewing submittals, attending meetings and site visits, and testing soil and fill. The amount is capped at $49,908.10, which includes a $4,537.10 contingency, for work from September 23, 2021 to December 31, 2023.

output.headline: Pays N.V. Heathorn Company $16,346 for steam pipe and tank repairs at The Center at Foster
output.summary: The district hires N.V. Heathorn Company to remove a stainless-steel chemical pipe from the steam header and cap it, then reconnect piping to the feed water tank with a new check valve and repaired insulation, as described in the company's July 12, 2021 proposal. The amount is $16,346.00, for work from September 23, 2021 to December 31, 2021.

output.headline: Appoints a district representative to the BayTech Charter School governing board
output.summary: On the recommendation of the Charters Committee, the Board appoints Shannon Ortland as the district's representative on the governing board of BayTech Charter School. The text states no dollar amount.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $20,400 for medical coverage at Oakland Athletic League high school sports

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $20,400.00

output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, a contract with an individual contractor to schedule and provide approved medical personnel at high school sports events run by the Oakland Athletic League. It covers up to 340 hours at $60.00 per hour, with a cap of $20,400.00, for July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022.

output.headline: Adds $48,134.11 to Redgwick's Sherman Elementary playground matting contract
output.summary: This change order adds $48,134.11 for new pieces added to a play structure so it suits ages 2 to 12 at Sherman Elementary School. It raises the contract from $203,900.00 to $252,034.11 and extends the term by 197 days to May 31, 2021. The contract term began September 16, 2020, before this approval.

output.headline: Accepts $58,200 more from Oakland Fund for Children and Youth for Summer Pre-K, through May 2022
output.summary: The district accepts an additional $58,200.00 from the City of Oakland's Oakland Fund for Children and Youth for the OUSD Summer Pre-K Program. This raises the grant from $199,087.00 to $257,287.00 and extends the grant period, which began July 1, 2019, from May 31, 2021 to May 31, 2022.

output.headline: Expands T-Mobile hot spot service to 10,000 student lines, up to $2,334,000 through 2026
output.summary: This amendment replaces a section of the district's agreement with T-Mobile USA, Inc. so T-Mobile can provide more student hot spot and cellular service, for a combined total of 10,000 lines. It runs from September 23, 2021 through June 30, 2026, with a total cap of $2,334,000.00 and no more than $466,800.00 per year. The text gives only the new overall cap, not how much this amendment adds.

output.headline: Creates a new job description for Supervisor, Warehouse and Distribution
output.summary: The Board adopts Resolution No. 2122-0058, which creates a job description for the position of Supervisor, Warehouse and Distribution. The text states no dollar amount or dates.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost agreement with Leaders Up for job search help for adult education students
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, a no-cost agreement with Leaders Up for job search help and hiring events that connect employers with Oakland Adult and Career Education students. The agreement runs from July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2024 at no cost to the district.

output.headline: Approves a no-cost agreement with Love Never Fails to provide adult education instructors
output.summary: The district agrees to have Love Never Fails provide instructors for College and Career Readiness classes for Oakland Adult and Career Education students, for agreed-upon hours. The agreement runs from July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2024 at no cost to the district.

output.headline: Approves a 30-year lease with Trust for Public Land for a green schoolyard at Bridges Academy
output.summary: The district enters a 30-year lease with Trust for Public Land, from September 9, 2021 to September 9, 2051. The lease is meant to help the organization win a state park grant (Statewide Park Program Proposition 68) so it can do community outreach, design and build green schoolyard improvements at Bridges Academy. The text states no dollar amount.

output.headline: Ratifies the minutes of the Board's August 11, 2021 regular meeting
output.summary: The Board approves the written minutes of its regular meeting held August 11, 2021. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting.

output.headline: Ratifies the minutes of the Board's August 25, 2021 regular meeting
output.summary: The Board approves the written minutes of its regular meeting held August 25, 2021. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting.
